thread:
jen_support: FYI we got a high-sev from Acme about streaming responses timing out mid-stream and clients showing partial outputs. customer says it started after they moved behind a corporate proxy. ticket 98432.

owen_sre: Can you paste the client's basic repro? headers, timings, anything.

jen_support: Customer sent this quick repro: `curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=gpt-x` — they see an initial event(s) then the connection drops after ~90s. Sometimes client reconnects and gets only partial final chunk.

maya_eng: Important q: are they using ALB / Cloud HTTP proxy in front? If so, ALB idle timeout default is 60s/idle which can cause half-closed TCPs.
\jen_support: They confirmed AWS ALB in front plus a corporate proxy that also does TLS interception.
\nora_solutions: Common pattern: client sees SSE keepalive as comments, but intermediate proxies/balancers drop idle connections if no actual bytes for idle window. If our server only sends KV/cache-backed tokens (small) periodically, those may get aggregated/lost.

owen_sre: Captured server logs from the customer timeframe: `conn=cid-0a1b2c state=streaming sent=842 last_activity=2025-10-12T15:03:45Z evt=token_flush` then `conn=cid-0a1b2c state=half-closed tcp_close=RST` — RST from upstream.

kyle_runtime: Can we see proxy/ALB access logs? need to know if ALB sends close or if the client's proxy is initiating.

jen_support: Customer attached ALB logs snippet: `2025-10-12T15:04:20.123Z alb-id elb-xyz 10.0.0.12:443 192.0.2.14:52344 0.001 90.001 0.000 200 200 0 12345 \"GET https://api.../v1/stream HTTP/1.1\"` 

maya_eng: That 90s stands out. Looks like ALB counted a long backend processing time. ALB has an idle timeout of 60s by default on some setups; vendor proxies can also forcibly close after 90s. If there's a midstream micro-burst or we rely on TCP keepalives only, that may not keep the connection 'fresh' for ALB/proxy.

nora_solutions: Two orthogonal mechanisms for liveness: TCP-level keepalive (OS-level probes) and application-level heartbeat (SSE comment pings `: ping\n\n`).

TCP keepalive intervals are usually very long (hours) unless tuned; not reliable for short timeouts. Recommendation is application-level comment pings at an interval < min(idle_timeout) / 2.

owen_sre: Quick experiment idea: Have server send `:keepalive\n\n` every 20s as SSE comment. Also have client send an occasional HTTP-level OPTIONS preflight? (probably not helpful).

jen_support: Customer asked whether comment pings count as activity for ALB / corporate proxies. Anyone seen differences between comment pings vs small data frames?

maya_eng: In our ops we've found that most HTTP proxies consider any bytes on the wire as activity. SSE comment `:\n` emits bytes. However some proxies do deep-inspection and might buffer until a newline or limit before forwarding; TLS interception can also interact. The safe pattern is to emit a small non-empty SSE event every N seconds, e.g.:

```
: keepalive

event: rtt
data: {"ts": "2025-10-12T15:04:00Z"}

```

This gives both bytes and structured event for clients.

kyle_runtime: Also important: if we emit only SSE comments (colon lines), some upstreams may normalize or strip comment-only frames for optimization. Emitting a tiny data event (like `{}`) is more robust.

jen_support: Customer tried turning on a client-side poll every 30s (new TCP connection) and they said it reduced disconnects but increased billing and created duplicate partial outputs. We need a fix that doesn't force duplicate charges.

nora_solutions: For billing: we should treat reconnections with `Last-Event-ID` or a server-side session token to dedupe charging. We already support `last_event_id` for resume in some models; confirm for streaming.

maya_eng: Code-level note: our runtime flush intervals can batch tokens and delay bytes until a chunk is full. For streaming SLOs we should flush partial token batches more frequently when stream clients are detected or when `stream=true` query param is present.

nowen_sre: (reacts :thumbsup:)

jen_support: Customer asked for repro steps we can provide them. Any compact script?

maya_eng: Minimal Node repro that forces policy:

```js
const https = require('https');
const req = https.request({
  hostname: 'api.redwood.example',
  path: '/v1/stream?model=gpt-x',
  headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer ...', 'Accept': 'text/event-stream' }
});
req.on('data', chunk => process.stdout.write(chunk));
req.end();
// simulate slow network by delaying server token flush on our test service
```

jen_support: I'll send that. Also customer asked whether switching to WebSocket helps.

kyle_runtime: WebSockets maintain a persistent bi-directional channel; they still rely on intermediate proxies and will be subject to same idle timeouts. However many proxies treat WS differently (upgrade keeps connection open) — but not guaranteed. If going WS, still send application-level pings (`ping/pong`) and have session resume.

nora_solutions: Agreed. For long-lived streams recommend: application-level heartbeat (data event), smaller flush windows on runtime, resumable stream semantics (last-event-id / session token) to avoid double-billing, and guidance to customers on configuring ALB/proxy idle timeouts.

owen_sre: Operational quick wins we can do today: 1) In-host default: emit `event:_hb` data `{}` every 20s for SSE streams behind known partners. 2) Add an opt-in header `x-redwood-heartbeat: comment`/`data` to let clients choose. 3) Document known ALB settings and corporate proxies in our support KB.

maya_eng: I'll open an internal RFC to change default flush/heartbeat behavior in the runtime. Need to check perf impact for high-throughput customers — will gate by customer tier / route config.

jen_support: Customer also reported partial outputs on reconnect (they saw the same last token repeated). We should include dedupe guidance.

kyle_runtime: For dedupe: attach a server-generated stream-session-id on the initial connect and increment an offset for each emitted event. Client includes `Last-Event-ID` or `x-redwood-session` on reconnect. Server will mark already-billed offsets to avoid recharging. This needs product + billing signoff.

nora_solutions: I'll loop in billing and product after we validate repro.

jen_support: Customer asked for immediate mitigation steps they can try today — what to tell them?

nowen_sre: Ask them to: 1) enable client-side heartbeat (emit a tiny SSE data event) every 15-20s, not only comments. 2) raise ALB/proxy idle timeout to >120s if possible. 3) switch to a single reconnect strategy that includes `Last-Event-ID` header and avoids multiple parallel reconnects.

jen_support: I'll send those steps + Node repro. Also will request ALB logs covering the windows.

deploy-bot: Note: created issue RNF-1283 (runtime: SSE heartbeat defaults) assigned to maya_eng.

maya_eng: Thanks — I'll prototype server-side heartbeat and shorter token flush for stream routes. Will post a perf/regression test plan.

jen_support: Thanks all — customer is trying the client-side heartbeat now. keeping this thread open for logs and confirmation. :pray:

sre-bot: Incident monitor attached: stream-drop-rate spike detected between 2025-10-12T15:00 and 15:10 UTC, correlation id=spike-198765

jen_support: Update from customer 20m later: after adding small data heartbeats every 20s they saw a stable connection for 25+ minutes, no duplicate charges yet. They will send full logs tomorrow.

maya_eng: Great. We'll track RNF-1283 progress and follow up with docs + server-side opt-in.

kyle_runtime: Also leaving note: test internal e2e across common corp proxies (Bluecoat, Zscaler) — some rewrite or buffering behaviors differ.

jen_support: Closing for now, will reopen if logs show server closes. Thanks team.
